steps.title: Prepare MOPS stock solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 20.9 g MOPS in de‑ionised water, top up to 100 mL, adjust pH to 7.0 with 5 M HCl, keep at 4 °C; shelf‑life ≈6 months. (Sigma catalog 106129)

steps.title: Prepare Tricine stock solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 17.9 g Tricine in de‑ionised water, top up to 100 mL, adjust pH to 7.8 with 5 M HCl, keep at 4 °C; shelf‑life ≈6 months. (AppliChem catalog A10585)

steps.title: Prepare KCl stock solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 224 g KCl in de‑ionised water, top up to 100 mL (3 M); store at 24 °C, unlimited shelf‑life. (Sigma catalog P9541)

steps.title: Prepare Ascorbate stock solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 198 mg L‑ascorbic acid in de‑ionised water, top up to 1 mL (1 M); keep in a dark tube and prepare fresh on the day of experiment; short lifespan. (Sigma catalog 255564)

steps.title: Prepare MgCl₂ stock solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 2.38 g MgCl₂·6H₂O in de‑ionised water, top up to 100 mL (1 M); keep at 4 °C, unlimited shelf‑life. (Sigma catalog M8266)

steps.title: Prepare t‑PCCαM stock solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1 g trans‑PCC α‑maltoside in hot de‑ionised water, top up to 10 mL (10 % w/v); aliquot into 1 mL tubes and store at –20 °C (≈6 months). (Glycon catalog D99019)

steps.title: Make JTS activity solution (JAs)
steps.instruction: Mix MOPS stock to give 30 mM final concentration, add t‑PCCαM to 0.01 % (v/v), bring volume to 1 L with de‑ionised water; keep at 4 °C, shelf‑life 2–3 months.

steps.title: Make Cyt b₆f purification solution (CPs)
steps.instruction: Add 100 mL of 30 mM KCl stock (Recipe 3) to the JAs solution; keep at 4 °C, shelf‑life 2–3 months.

steps.title: Make PSI purification solution (PPs)
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL of 1 M MgCl₂ stock (Recipe 5) to the JAs solution to obtain 5 mM final MgCl₂; keep at 4 °C, shelf‑life 2–3 months.

steps.title: Make Plastocyanin column buffer (PC‑B)
steps.instruction: Add 25 mL of 1 M Tricine stock (Recipe 2) to obtain 25 mM Tricine, add 3.3 mL of 3 M KCl stock (Recipe 3) to obtain 10 mM KCl, top up with de‑ionised water to 1 L; keep at 4 °C, shelf‑life ≈6 months.

steps.title: Thaw purified protein complexes
steps.instruction: Retrieve PSI, Cyt b₆f, recombinant PC and FDX aliquots stored at –80 °C, thaw on ice and keep on ice until use.

steps.title: Assemble assay mixture in cuvette
steps.instruction: In a 1 mL quartz cuvette add JAs buffer to a final volume of 400 µL, supplement with ascorbate to 10 mM, MgCl₂ to 2.5 mM and KCl to 7.5 mM. Then add PSI to 250 nM (per reaction centre), Cyt b₆f to 2.13 µM and PC (recombinant) to 1 µM. Prepare a control lacking Cyt b₆f. Adjust PSI concentration as required (e.g., 50 nM RC) based on chlorophyll quantification (217 Chl per PSI RC).

steps.title: Perform PC and FDX titrations
steps.instruction: Add ferredoxin (FDX) to final concentrations of 0.5, 1, 2 and 4 µM and plastocyanin (PC) to 2, 3, 4 and 5 µM sequentially for the respective experimental sets.

steps.title: Configure spectroscopic instrument
steps.instruction: Install the Biologic “Smart Lamp” LED system, remove all physical filters from the detector path, and set detector balance to “Automatic”. Set all detection voltages to 5 V and verify that no reference channel exceeds 10 V. Twist the Smart Lamp if needed to increase signal voltage for the 554 nm (and, if used, 705 nm) reference measurements.

steps.title: Program measurement sequence
steps.instruction:
Enter the following sequence command into the JTS‑150 software (exact string as published):

20(50msD)T4(10(200msD)A[on]10usA[off]140usB[on]10usB[off]2000usD10(200msD)3(20(50msD)A[on]10usA[off]140usB[on]10usB[off]1140us{700us,100,5s,D})10(200msD)20(50msD){1200us,100,2s,H350usD50usG[8000uE]}H{1200us,200,20s,D})

This program executes four laser flashes (first flash for laser stabilisation), an initial 700 µs delay, a mandatory 2 ms delay before the first probe pulse, a 2 s dark pause, a 2 s actinic illumination (orange light, 350 µE m⁻² s⁻¹), and a 20 s dark recovery. The sequence is repeated for four technical replicates.

steps.title: Acquire absorbance data
steps.instruction: Record absorbance continuously at 546, 554, 563, 573, 705 and 740 nm throughout the entire sequence for each technical replicate.

steps.title: Perform spectral deconvolution and baseline correction
steps.instruction:
Using the recorded data, apply a linear baseline correction with the two reference wavelengths (546 nm and 573 nm) where cytochrome absorbance is redox‑independent. Then correct the Cyt f trace by subtracting 27 % of the 563 nm signal:

D₅₅₄* = D₅₄₆ – 0.27 × D₅₆₃ – D₅₄₆

For every detection point calculate a linear slope between D₅₄₆ and D₅₇₃ and obtain the corrected baseline value (D_corr) for the target wavelength (WL) using:

WL_corr = WL × (D₅₄₆ – D₅₇₃) / (546 – 573) + D₅₄₆ – WL × (546 – 573) / (546 – 573)

(Exact formula reproduced from the protocol.)

steps.title: Isolate individual redox signals
steps.instruction:
Calculate the final corrected signals:

Cyt f = D₅₅₄* – 554_corr
Cyt b = D₅₆₃ – 563_corr
P700 = D₇₀₅ – D₇₄₀

steps.title: Average technical replicates
steps.instruction: Average the 12 measurements (3 data flashes × 4 technical replicates) to improve signal‑to‑noise ratio for Cyt f, Cyt b and P700 traces.

steps.title: Fit kinetic phases
steps.instruction: Fit the actinic‑light (AL) phase (the 2 s illumination) with a double‑exponential decay: fast phase t₁⁄₂ ≈ 10 ms, slow phase t₁⁄₂ ≈ 500 ms. Fit the post‑actinic dark phase (20 s) with a single‑exponential decay representing FDX‑mediated re‑reduction of Cyt f.
